
candidates.claim: `isMulCommutative_mono` is misnamed: its statement is the *antitone* (downward-closed) direction — from `h : s ≤ t` and `[IsMulCommutative t]` it deduces `IsMulCommutative s`, i.e. commutativity of the *larger* subobject is inherited by the *smaller* one. Mathlib spells this direction `anti` (compare `Set.Subsingleton.anti` `(ht : t.Subsingleton) (hst : s ⊆ t) : s.Subsingleton`, `SimpleGraph.Simple.anti (hle : H ≤ G) : H.Simple`, `SimpleGraph.Loopless.anti [hG : G.Loopless] (hle : H ≤ G) : H.Loopless`, `SimpleGraph.CliqueFree.anti (h : G ≤ H) : H.CliqueFree n → G.CliqueFree n`, `SimpleGraph.IsAcyclic.anti (hsub : G ≤ G') (h : G'.IsAcyclic) : G.IsAcyclic`, `IsIntersectingOf.anti`, `Filter.Subsingleton.anti`), whereas `mono` is reserved for the opposite, upward-closed direction (`Set.Nontrivial.mono`, `ConvexCone.Pointed.mono`, `IsIntersectingOf.mono`). The PR title itself announces the declaration as `isMulCommutative_anti`, so the code does not provide the advertised name; the docstring ("Commutativity of multiplication passes to smaller subobjects.") also describes the antitone direction and so is inconsistent with `_mono`.
